`abstract class LineFieldNode<V>`<br/>
**Extends:** [`FieldNode<V>`](/reference/controls/fieldnode/)<br/>
**Known subtypes:** [`IntegerFieldNode`](/reference/controls/integerfieldnode/), [`TextFieldNode`](/reference/controls/textfieldnode/)<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.lib.ui.node.impl.control.field` · **Module:** `core` · **Source:** [LineFieldNode.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/core/src/main/java/dev/joid/lib/ui/node/impl/control/field/LineFieldNode.java)

A one-line field: Enter submits it, and its text scrolls sideways to follow the cursor.

## Description

Extend it for a field of your own value type: write `parse` and `format`, and `correct`, `accepts` or `increment` when the type needs them.
A field of height `0` takes the height of its font plus its top and bottom margins.

## Learn more

- [Text fields](/use/learn/interactivity/text-fields/#write-a-field-for-your-own-value)

## Event details

<a id="LineFieldNode-event-onSubmit"></a>

### onSubmit

`this onSubmit(EventListener<NodeEvent<T>> listener)` <span class="joid-qualifier">fluent</span>

Adds a listener that runs when the user presses Enter or the Enter of the keypad, after the field lost the focus.

---

<small>`fluent` returns the instance, typed for chaining · `factory` creates an instance · `signal` also accepts a value that follows signals, as a signal, an expression or a lambda ([When does JOID compute this value again?](/use/learn/interactivity/signals/#ask-when-does-joid-compute-this-value-again)) · `hook` called by JOID, override it · `abstract` you implement it · `default` interface method with a body · `static` called on the class · `protected` visible to subclasses</small>
